text: Carpentry constructs functional and beautiful structures by shaping and assembling wooden parts; it demands patience, precision, and close attention to detail. One essential action within this trade is sawing, where an artisan employs different blade types to form wood into specific shapes and dimensions. This operation may be succeeded by sanding, which levels the material to produce a smooth face. Yet the craft often diverges at this point because sanding cannot serve as the main task. Rather, it functions as a concluding measure that finalizes assembly, guaranteeing the finished object is strong, stable, and visually attractive. While sawing and sanding belong to the overall procedure, they do not define its core purpose.
